messages:
emma_support: Heads up — OrbitPay is reporting elevated 5xxs and truncated responses since ~08:12 UTC. They also saw a billing spike. I dug into a sample trace: the request was routed to eu-standby and served model 'gpt-lite-v2-q8' instead of the expected 'gpt-pro-v1'.

ingest_bot: [alert] route-failover: region=eu, probe=auth, routed_to=eu-standby, fallback_variant=gpt-lite-v2-q8, request_id=orbp-0a12b3

raj_oncall: Can you paste the raw request/response headers + request id? Also, did the customer include any custom model_preferences in their call?

emma_support: Sample below (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Region: eu
X-Customer-Org: orbitpay
Body: {"model":"gpt-pro-v1","input":"Summarize invoice #123"}

Response headers:
X-Model-Served: gpt-lite-v2-q8
X-Tokenizer-Tag: bpe-lite-vocab-8000
X-Request-Id: orbp-0a12b3
Content-Length: 42

Response body: "Invoice summary: [TRUNCATED]"
```

sara_ml: That header combo is the smoking gun. gpt-lite-v2 uses a reduced BPE vocab and different byte handling; it will produce shorter outputs and tokenization mismatches for prompts relying on certain special tokens. The billing jump could be retries + downstream client resends after truncated body.

thomas_platform: How did routing decide to fallback to the lite variant? Our policy should only pick a reduced-capability variant when sequence-length and model-compatibility checks pass.

raj_oncall: Repro steps I ran locally:
1) Replicated auth-probe to eu primary to force standby promotion.
2) Sent the same payload with org=orbitpay (their org is pinned to pro but fallback rules allowed lite).
3) Observed same X-Model-Served header.

Quick mitigation: set org-level routing override for orbitpay to prefer model_id exact-match until we patch. I can push a temporary rule.

emma_support: Customer wants refund/credits for the billing spike. They say some invoices got processed twice because the truncated output caused retries.

thomas_platform: Action items:
- raj_oncall: roll temporary org-level routing override (priority: now).
- sara_ml: add compatibility check in routing decision so tokenizer/tag is considered when choosing fallback variants.
- emma_support: confirm credit amount and propose remediation to the customer.
- I'll open an internal incident and link the change PR.

sara_ml: For long-term fix, we need:
- a compatibility matrix: model_variant x tokenizer_tag -> allowed_fallbacks
- a preflight header check: if served_variant.tokenizer != expected.tokenizer then reject and route to next available compatible node, not the lite fallback.

raj_oncall: Implemented temporary override at 08:48 UTC, pushed rule id=tmp-orbitpay-pin-202312. Monitoring now.

ingest_bot: [deploy] routing-change tmp-orbitpay-pin-202312 applied by raj_oncall at 08:48 UTC (propagated 15s)

emma_support: Customer responded: appreciate fast response. They asked what prevented this from being caught by our health checks.

thomas_platform: We only health-check node liveness and a generic model health ping; we don't assert variant/tokenizer compatibility on failover. That's the gap. Ticket created: INT-6543 (routing compatibility + preflight).

sara_ml: Small repro snippet to catch this in test harness:
```python
# simulate routing probe + request to standby
def send_request():
    h = {"Authorization":"Bearer X","X-Region":"eu","X-Customer-Org":"orbitpay"}
    body = {"model":"gpt-pro-v1","input":"test special_token: ©"}
    r = requests.post(url, headers=h, json=body)
    return r.headers.get('X-Model-Served'), r.headers.get('X-Tokenizer-Tag'), r.text
```

Use this to add an assertion in canary that served_tokenizer == expected_tokenizer.

raj_oncall: Monitoring shows error rate decreased after override. Billing spike mitigation: ops billing team will issue credit for the duplicated charges. emma_support, please coordinate quoting credit amount.

emma_support: Will do. I'll ask billing to prepare a provisional credit and send a note to OrbitPay.

thomas_platform: Leaving notes: escalate to postmortem if action items not resolved within 72h. P0 until compatibility check is in prod.

sara_ml: I'll start a PR for the compatibility matrix and preflight check. Tagging @thomas_platform and @raj_oncall for design review.

raj_oncall: TL;DR: Region auth probe caused requests to route to standby; standby was allowed to serve a lower-capacity lite variant that uses a different tokenizer. That mismatch caused truncated outputs -> client retries -> billing spike. Temporary org pin is live; long term we add tokenizer compatibility to routing and canary preflight.

emma_support: Thanks everyone. I'll update the customer thread and log this incident. :thumbsup:
